topic.title: Recurrent Sequence Models and Structured State Spaces
topic.overview: Recurrent models summarize a sequence in a state that is updated over time. This topic studies long-term memory, stable optimization, gating, structured recurrences, and reservoir computing. The challenge is to retain useful history without making parameter updates unstable or forcing prohibitively slow sequential computation.
topic.whyItMatters: Vanishing and exploding gradients are only part of the difficulty: a model with long memory can also be extremely sensitive to small parameter changes. Structured parameterizations can improve both optimization and parallel computation, but must preserve enough expressiveness for the sequence patterns of interest.
topic.evolution: Early representatives explore recurrent associative memory and sequential structure. Later work adds orthogonal, gated, and dilated designs. A 2024 analysis links long-memory optimization difficulties to parameter sensitivity beyond gradient explosion; ParalESN in 2026 uses complex diagonal linear recurrences to parallelize reservoir processing while preserving stated echo-state and universality properties.
openQuestions: Which recurrence structures best balance long memory with stable parameter learning?
How can parallel sequence processing retain sensitivity to irregular or nonstationary events?

papers.title: MomentumRNN: Integrating Momentum into Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.tldr: MomentumRNN incorporates momentum into recurrent hidden-state dynamics, alleviating vanishing gradients and improving performance in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Regularizing Towards Permutation Invariance In Recurrent Models
papers.tldr: Stochastic regularization lets recurrent models learn full or partial insensitivity to input order and can yield compact, effective models.

papers.title: Reservoir Computing meets Recurrent Kernels and Structured Transforms
papers.tldr: A proven recurrent-kernel limit and a structured-reservoir alternative improve the speed and memory efficiency of reservoir computing.

papers.title: Stable and expressive recurrent vision models
papers.tldr: C-RBP trains recurrent vision models with memory constant in the number of recurrent steps and shows strong contour-tracing and segmentation results.

papers.title: STLnet: Signal Temporal Logic Enforced Multivariate Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.tldr: STLnet uses temporal logic to guide sequential neural models toward accurate, robust predictions that satisfy specified model properties.

papers.title: Training Linear Finite-State Machines
papers.tldr: Trainable finite-state-machine networks support multiplication-free stochastic computation and temporal learning with reported memory and power savings over LSTMs.

papers.title: Implicit Bias of Linear RNNs
papers.tldr: Infinite-width linear RNNs behave like weighted convolutions biased toward recent inputs, explaining a form of short-memory learning.

papers.title: MC-LSTM: Mass-Conserving LSTM
papers.tldr: MC-LSTM builds conservation into recurrent memory, achieving strong arithmetic and hydrology results with interpretable states in the hydrology application.

papers.title: Modeling Hierarchical Structures with Continuous Recursive Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Continuous relaxation lets recursive neural networks learn latent hierarchies through backpropagation, with strong results on structured language tasks.

papers.title: Parallelizing Legendre Memory Unit Training
papers.tldr: A simplified Legendre Memory Unit enables parallel training with reported speedups up to 200 times while retaining recurrent inference and improving benchmark accuracy.

papers.title: Training Recurrent Neural Networks via Forward Propagation Through Time
papers.tldr: FPTT trains recurrent networks through sequential updates with a dynamic regularizer, supporting stationary convergence and improved benchmark performance.

papers.title: UnICORNN: A recurrent model for learning very long time dependencies
papers.tldr: UnICORNN uses structure-preserving oscillator dynamics to mitigate gradient problems and learn very long sequence dependencies.

papers.title: Combining Recurrent, Convolutional, and Continuous-time Models with Linear State Space Layers
papers.tldr: Linear State-Space Layers connect recurrent, convolutional, and continuous-time sequence models while supporting effective long-range memory.

papers.title: DeepSITH: Efficient Learning via Decomposition of What and When Across Time Scales
papers.tldr: DeepSITH represents events at logarithmically spaced delays to learn temporal relationships across a wide range of timescales.

papers.title: Framing RNN as a kernel method: A neural ODE approach
papers.tldr: Under suitable conditions, a continuous-time view expresses RNN solutions as kernel methods and yields generalization and stability guarantees.

papers.title: Going Beyond Linear Transformers with Recurrent Fast Weight Programmers
papers.tldr: Adding recurrence to fast weight programmers extends linear Transformer architectures and produces large reported gains over LSTM in several Atari games.

papers.title: Learning and Generalization in RNNs
papers.tldr: New proof techniques show that RNNs can learn broader sequence functions by making information in their hidden states accessible to analysis.

papers.title: Reverse engineering recurrent neural networks with Jacobian switching linear dynamical systems
papers.tldr: Co-training an RNN with a switching linear model makes its dynamics easier to interpret while maintaining a close approximation.

papers.title: SBO-RNN: Reformulating Recurrent Neural Networks via Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
papers.tldr: SBO-RNN derives recurrent networks from bilevel optimization, with conditional gradient-stability guarantees and reported gains in performance and training efficiency.

papers.title: Self-Instantiated Recurrent Units with Dynamic Soft Recursion
papers.tldr: Self-IRU adds gated, dynamically varying soft recursion to recurrent networks and demonstrates strong performance across multiple data modalities.

papers.title: Structured in Space, Randomized in Time: Leveraging Dropout in RNNs for Efficient Training
papers.tldr: Structuring dropout across batches turns LSTM sparsity into reported training speedups of 1.23–1.64 times without sacrificing task metrics.

papers.title: Turing Completeness of Bounded-Precision Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A 54-neuron bounded-precision RNN with dynamically growing memory can simulate a Universal Turing Machine with linear-time overhead.

papers.title: Understanding Adaptive, Multiscale Temporal Integration In Deep Speech Recognition Systems
papers.tldr: Context-based measurements reveal that trained speech networks progress from short time-based integration windows to longer windows aligned with speech structure.

papers.title: A deep convolutional neural network that is invariant to time rescaling
papers.tldr: SITHCon uses logarithmic temporal memory to recognize learned time-series patterns across substantial changes in playback speed.

papers.title: Recurrent Model-Free RL Can Be a Strong Baseline for Many POMDPs
papers.tldr: Carefully configured recurrent model-free reinforcement learning beats specialized comparisons in sample efficiency and final performance on 18 of 21 tested environments.

papers.title: Understanding Robust Generalization in Learning Regular Languages
papers.tldr: Predicting intermediate automaton states helps recurrent networks generalize regular languages under distribution shifts.

papers.title: Block-Recurrent Transformers
papers.tldr: A transformer that recurrently processes token blocks improves long-sequence language modeling while keeping complexity linear in sequence length.

papers.title: Explain My Surprise: Learning Efficient Long-Term Memory by predicting uncertain outcomes
papers.tldr: MemUP uses locally uncertain predictions to guide long-term memory learning while reducing stored training intermediates in reported LSTM experiments.

papers.title: On the difficulty of learning chaotic dynamics with RNNs
papers.tldr: The paper links RNN gradient divergence to chaotic dynamics through Lyapunov spectra and uses that connection to guide training.

papers.title: On the Parameterization and Initialization of Diagonal State Space Models
papers.tldr: Carefully initialized diagonal state space models retain much of S4's performance while greatly simplifying kernel computation.

papers.title: Online Neural Sequence Detection with Hierarchical Dirichlet Point Process
papers.tldr: A hierarchical Dirichlet point process detects neural sequences online and adds new sequence types as needed.

papers.title: Temporal Latent Bottleneck: Synthesis of Fast and Slow Processing Mechanisms in Sequence Learning
papers.tldr: A recurrent slow stream and Transformer fast stream combine temporal compression with expressive processing, improving results on tested sequence tasks.

papers.title: Adaptive Computation with Elastic Input Sequence
papers.tldr: AdaTape adapts input sequence content and length to improve image recognition performance at maintained computational cost.

papers.title: Beam Tree Recursive Cells
papers.tldr: BT-Cell makes beam search compatible with training recursive networks, achieving strong structural-task results while exposing a specific generalization failure.

papers.title: EM-Network: Oracle Guided Self-distillation for Sequence Learning
papers.tldr: EM-Network transfers the benefits of target-derived oracle guidance into sequence models through one-stage self-distillation.

papers.title: Resurrecting Recurrent Neural Networks for Long Sequences
papers.tldr: The Linear Recurrent Unit uses carefully designed linear recurrence to match deep state-space models' Long Range Arena performance and efficiency.

papers.title: Scalable Adaptive Computation for Iterative Generation
papers.tldr: RIN routes data through recurrent latent computation, enabling high-resolution pixel diffusion with reported efficiency gains of up to tenfold over U-Nets.

papers.title: Sequence Modeling with Multiresolution Convolutional Memory
papers.tldr: MultiresLayer uses shared multiscale convolutions to model long sequences efficiently while achieving strong results on several sequence tasks.

papers.title: Balancing memorization and generalization in RNNs for high performance brain-machine Interfaces
papers.tldr: Recurrent decoders improve real-time finger control in primate BMI experiments by combining continuous decoding with learned movement patterns.

papers.title: Bifurcations and loss jumps in RNN training
papers.tldr: The paper links certain RNN bifurcations to extreme gradients and introduces an algorithm for analyzing the dynamics behind training instability.

papers.title: Convolutional State Space Models for Long-Range Spatiotemporal Modeling
papers.tldr: ConvS5 combines spatially structured states with efficient sequence computation to improve long-range prediction and generation.

papers.title: Decoding the Enigma: Benchmarking Humans and AIs on the Many Facets of Working Memory
papers.tldr: WorM benchmarks multiple working-memory abilities and finds that tested AI models reproduce some, but not all, human behavioral characteristics.

papers.title: Efficient Beam Tree Recursion
papers.tldr: Separating scoring from recursive computation cuts BT-RvNN memory use by 10–16 times and enables contextual outputs for individual tokens.

papers.title: Hierarchically Gated Recurrent Neural Network for Sequence Modeling
papers.tldr: HGRN uses increasingly restrictive forget-gate bounds across layers to support local processing below and longer-term memory above.

papers.title: Online learning of long-range dependencies
papers.tldr: Independent recurrent modules enable competitive online learning of long-range dependencies at twice the memory and computation of a single inference pass.

papers.title: Recursion in Recursion: Two-Level Nested Recursion for Length Generalization with Scalability
papers.tldr: RIR nests flexible recursion inside a balanced tree to combine strong ListOps length generalization with scalable long-sequence processing.

papers.title: State-space models with layer-wise nonlinearity are universal approximators with exponential decaying memory
papers.tldr: Layer-wise nonlinearities make stacked state-space models universal approximators, while exponentially decaying memory remains.

papers.title: A Tensor Decomposition Perspective on Second-order RNNs
papers.tldr: CPRNN uses tensor decomposition to make second-order recurrent networks compact, with strong results when rank and hidden size are chosen appropriately.

papers.title: Learning Useful Representations of Recurrent Neural Network Weight Matrices
papers.tldr: Probing RNN behavior produces useful weight representations and clearly improves identification of training tasks in the paper's hardest evaluation.

papers.title: StableSSM: Alleviating the Curse of Memory in State-space Models through Stable Reparameterization
papers.tldr: StableSSM uses reparameterization to lift a proven stable-memory limitation of state-space models and can also improve optimization stability.

papers.title: State-Free Inference of State-Space Models: The *Transfer Function* Approach
papers.tldr: A transfer-function parameterization enables state-free sequence processing and reports faster training and improved performance on sequence-modeling benchmarks.

papers.title: The Illusion of State in State-Space Models
papers.tldr: The paper finds that the analyzed state-space models share transformers' formal state-tracking limitations, supported by experiments with Mamba-style models.

papers.title: Universality of Linear Recurrences Followed by Non-linear Projections: Finite-Width Guarantees and Benefits of Complex Eigenvalues
papers.tldr: Linear diagonal recurrences followed by nonlinear projections are universal for regular causal sequence maps, while suitable complex eigenvalues improve information storage.

papers.title: NeuralSolver: Learning Algorithms For Consistent and Efficient Extrapolation Across General Tasks
papers.tldr: NeuralSolver learns on smaller problems and more effectively extrapolates to larger ones, including tasks with unequal input and output sizes.

papers.title: Real-Time Recurrent Learning using Trace Units in Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: Recurrent Trace Units enable efficient online recurrent learning and outperform evaluated alternatives in several partially observable reinforcement-learning environments.

papers.title: Recurrent neural networks: vanishing and exploding gradients are not the end of the story
papers.tldr: Longer recurrent memory can amplify output sensitivity to parameter changes even without exploding gradients, while element-wise recurrence and careful parameterization help mitigate it.

papers.title: Segment, Shuffle, and Stitch: A Simple Layer for Improving Time-Series Representations
papers.tldr: S3 learns to rearrange time-series segments and blend them with the original sequence to improve representations and training stability.

papers.title: The Expressive Capacity of State Space Models: A Formal Language Perspective
papers.tldr: A formal-language analysis identifies state space models' strengths in state tracking and bounded hierarchy, alongside a design-related expressivity limit.

papers.title: Understanding the Differences in Foundation Models: Attention, State Space Models, and Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A shared dynamical-systems framework clarifies differences, conditional equivalences, and approximation relationships among major sequence-model architectures.

papers.title: Universal In-Context Approximation By Prompting Fully Recurrent Models
papers.tldr: The paper proves that several fully recurrent architectures can be universal in-context approximators and identifies gating as helpful for stable implementations.

papers.title: A Large Recurrent Action Model: xLSTM enables Fast Inference for Robotics Tasks
papers.tldr: LRAM uses xLSTM to combine fast recurrent inference with competitive action-model performance across 432 tasks.

papers.title: Algorithm Development in Neural Networks: Insights from the Streaming Parity Task
papers.tldr: On streaming parity, recurrent networks can transition from finite training experience to perfect arbitrary-length generalization through a representational merger resembling a finite automaton.

papers.title: Implicit Language Models are RNNs: Balancing Parallelization and Expressivity
papers.tldr: Implicit state-space models recover nonlinear recurrent computation while largely retaining parallel training and improving reported benchmark performance.

papers.title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
papers.tldr: Test-Time Training layers use a learnable model as recurrent memory, enabling continued benefits from longer context with linear complexity.

papers.title: SKOLR: Structured Koopman Operator Linear RNN for Time-Series Forecasting
papers.tldr: SKOLR connects structured Koopman operators with linear recurrent networks to build a parallelizable time-series forecasting model.

papers.title: Understanding and Improving Length Generalization in Recurrent Models
papers.tldr: Broadening the internal states seen during training helps recurrent models handle much longer sequences with a small post-training budget.

papers.title: Blending Complementary Memory Systems in Hybrid Quadratic-Linear Transformers
papers.tldr: Combining precise attention memory with fast-weight memory can overcome weaknesses of either system when their information flow is designed well.

papers.title: Block-Biased Mamba for Long-Range Sequence Processing
papers.tldr: B₂S₆ modifies Mamba’s dynamics and biases to improve long-range processing while maintaining its language-modeling performance.

papers.title: Bridging Expressivity and Scalability with Adaptive Unitary SSMs
papers.tldr: AUSSM combines adaptive unitary recurrence with parallel training to expand state space models’ symbolic capabilities and support long-sequence tasks.

papers.title: DeltaProduct: Improving State-Tracking in Linear RNNs via Householder Products
papers.tldr: DeltaProduct makes multiple structured updates per token to improve linear recurrent networks' state tracking, language modeling, and length extrapolation.

papers.title: Fixed-Point RNNs: Interpolating from Diagonal to Dense
papers.tldr: Fixed-point formulations connect parallelizable diagonal RNNs to dense recurrence, enabling an efficiency–expressivity tradeoff at fixed parameter count.

papers.title: Improving Bilinear RNN with Closed-loop Control
papers.tldr: Comba applies state and output feedback to a bilinear recurrent architecture, reporting improved performance and computational efficiency on language and vision tasks.

papers.title: Metric Automata Theory: A Unifying Theory of RNNs
papers.tldr: Metric Automata Theory explains how robustness and numerical precision shape the sequence-recognition capabilities of recurrent architectures.

papers.title: Nonparametric Quantile Regression with ReLU-Activated Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Properly designed ReLU recurrent networks attain near-optimal quantile-estimation rates under stated structural and time-dependence assumptions.

papers.title: Parallelization of Non-linear State-Space Models: Scaling Up Liquid-Resistance Liquid-Capacitance Networks for Efficient Sequence Modeling
papers.tldr: LrcSSM uses a diagonal Jacobian to parallelize nonlinear recurrence while providing gradient stability and strong long-range forecasting results.

papers.title: pLSTM: parallelizable Linear Source Transition Mark networks
papers.tldr: pLSTMs extend parallelizable linear recurrence to directed acyclic graphs and demonstrate strong long-distance reasoning on structured data.

papers.title: Revisiting Bi-Linear State Transitions in Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Bilinear recurrent updates let hidden states actively shape computation and form a hierarchy suited to increasingly complex state-tracking tasks.

papers.title: Revisiting Glorot Initialization for Long-Range Linear Recurrences
papers.tldr: The paper shows long-sequence instability in Glorot-initialized linear recurrences and proposes a width-aware rescaling to control signal growth and decay.

papers.title: Sequence Modeling with Spectral Mean Flows
papers.tldr: Spectral mean flows combine operator-based sequence representations, tensor networks, and flow matching for tractable time-series generation.

papers.title: Structured Linear CDEs: Maximally Expressive and Parallel-in-Time Sequence Models
papers.tldr: SLiCEs use structured state transitions to preserve dense-matrix expressivity while enabling efficient sequence modeling.

papers.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
papers.tldr: Titans combines attention with learned long-term neural memory to use historical information and scale effectively to larger contexts in reported tests.

papers.title: An Algebraic View of the Expressivity of Recurrent Language Models
papers.tldr: An algebraic framework explains how arithmetic choices can fundamentally change a recurrent model's computational expressivity.

papers.title: Artificial Hippocampus Networks for Efficient Long-Context Modeling
papers.tldr: Artificial Hippocampus Networks compress older context into fixed-size memory while retaining recent attention, improving long-context efficiency and benchmark performance.

papers.title: ATLAS: Learning to Optimally Memorize the Context at Test Time
papers.tldr: Atlas improves recurrent context memory by optimizing it using current and past tokens while increasing capacity and memory-management expressiveness.

papers.title: Global Credit Assignment via Dynamical Criticality
papers.tldr: COLA uses correlations in critical recurrent dynamics to approximate global learning with local updates and memory independent of sequence length.

papers.title: Improving the Performance and Learning Stability of Parallelizable RNNs Designed for Ultra-Low Power Applications
papers.tldr: Cumulative state updates improve low-power recurrent models' gradient flow, training stability, and long-range memory performance while retaining analog-friendly properties.

papers.title: MuonSSM: Orthogonalizing State Space Models for Sequence Modeling
papers.tldr: MuonSSM conditions incoming memory updates to improve state space model stability and long-context performance while preserving parallel scan complexity.

papers.title: On the "Induction Bias" in Sequence Models
papers.tldr: Experiments find that Transformers learn state tracking less data-efficiently than recurrent models, even when training and evaluation distributions match.

papers.title: ParalESN: Enabling parallel information processing in Reservoir Computing
papers.tldr: ParalESN enables parallel reservoir computation through complex diagonal recurrences while preserving established echo-state and universality guarantees.

papers.title: Preconditioned DeltaNet: Curvature-aware Sequence Modeling for Linear Recurrences
papers.tldr: Preconditioned delta-rule recurrences incorporate regression curvature through efficient diagonal approximations, improving recall and language-modeling results.

papers.title: WaveSSM: Multiscale State-Space Models for Non-stationary Signal Attention
papers.tldr: WaveSSM uses temporally localized wavelet frames to improve state-space modeling of physiological signals and audio with transient dynamics.
